source_text: Quodsi et stadium contendas in scripturis nominari, sane obtinebis. sed quae in stadio geruntur, indigna conspectu tuo non negabis, pugnos et calces et colaphos et omnem, petulantiam manus et quamcumque humani oris, id est diuinae imaginis, depugnationem. non probabis usquam uanos cursus et iaculatus et saltus uaniores, nusquam tibi uires aut iniuriosae aut uanae placebunt, sed nec cura facticii corporis, ut plasticam dei supergressa, et propter Graeciae otium altiles, homines oderis. et palaestrica diaboli negotium est: primos homines diabolus elisit. ipse caestus colubrina uis est, tenax ad occupandum, tortuosa ad obligandum, liquida ad elabendum. nullus tibi coronarum usus est; quid de coronis uoluptates aucuparis?
thought_title: The stadium's vanities and the devil's wrestling
orientation: Tertullian is continuing his argument that each kind of show is condemned by Scripture, now turning from the theater to the stadium and its athletic contests.
pass_a_gloss: But if you should contend that the stadium also is named in the Scriptures, you will indeed win your point. But you will not deny that the things which are done in the stadium are unworthy of your sight: punches and kicks and blows and all the wantonness of the hand and every kind of fighting of the human face, that is, of the divine image. You will not approve anywhere vain running and throwing and vainer jumping; nowhere will strengths either injurious or vain please you, but neither will care for an artificially built body, as having surpassed the molding of God, and men fattened for the sake of Greece's leisure, please you. And wrestling is the devil's business: the devil threw down the first humans. The boxing glove itself is a serpentine force, gripping to seize, twisting to bind, fluid to slip away. You have no use for crowns; why do you hunt pleasures from crowns?

choices.why: The term refers to the wrestling-school art or athletic training; 'wrestling' captures the physical contest Tertullian is condemning without importing modern 'athletics' connotations.
The caestus was the leather hand-covering used in Roman boxing; 'boxing glove' is the clearest literal equivalent for a modern reader.
The phrase links the boxing glove to the serpent in Eden; 'serpentine force' preserves the adjective's snake-like quality and the noun's sense of power.
Plastica refers to the art of shaping or molding; 'molding of God' keeps the image of God as sculptor of the human body, which Tertullian contrasts with artificial bodily training.
Altilis means fattened or fed up, used of fowl; 'men fattened' preserves the contemptuous image of athletes as livestock fattened for Greek leisure.

pass_b_english: But if you insist that the stadium is named in Scripture, you will certainly win your point. Yet you will not deny that what goes on in the stadium is unworthy of your eyes: punches, kicks, blows, every wantonness of the hand, and all the fighting done to the human face, which is the divine image. You will never approve of vain races and javelin throws and even vainer jumps. Nowhere will strength that is either injurious or vain please you. Nor will you care for an artificially built body, since it surpasses the molding of God, and you will hate men fattened for the leisure of Greece. And wrestling is the devil's business: the devil first threw down the first human beings. The boxing glove itself is a serpentine force, clinging to seize, twisting to bind, slippery to escape. You have no use for crowns; why do you hunt for pleasures from crowns?

last_rejected.quote: the devil first threw down the first human beings
last_rejected.why: Latin says the devil selected the first humans; English adds the action ‘threw down’, changing the meaning.
last_rejected.fix: the devil first selected the first human beings
last_rejected.ruling: 'elisit' from 'elido' means to crush/throw down; 'selected' is not its normal range here.

polish.changed: Clarified the apposition about the human face as the divine image, rendered 'Greek leisure' as 'the leisure of Greece' to avoid obscurity, and smoothed the sentence rhythm while preserving every claim and qualification.

notes.quote: the fighting of the human face—that is, of the divine image
notes.why: Awkward apposition; 'human face' = 'divine image' is theological point but phrased oddly.
notes.fix: Recast: 'the fighting of the human face, which is the divine image'.

notes.quote: You will hate men fattened for Greek leisure
notes.why: 'Greek leisure' (otium) is obscure; means athletes trained in Greek-style exercise, but phrased oddly.
notes.fix: Clarify: 'men fattened by Greek-style training and leisure'.

notes.quote: wrestling is the devil's business: the devil first threw down the first human beings
notes.why: 'Threw down' suggests wrestling move, but devil 'threw down' Adam and Eve metaphorically; pun may be intended but is strained.
notes.fix: Keep but note wordplay: 'the devil first overthrew'.

problems.quote: You will never approve of empty races and javelin throws and even emptier jumps

edits.old: You will never approve of empty races and javelin throws and even emptier jumps.
edits.new: You will never approve of vain races and javelin throws and even vainer jumps.

fixed: Changed 'empty' to 'vain' to match the source's 'uanos' and 'uaniores', which the glossary renders as 'vain'.
